judged_text: In sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse returns data reduced to {access_token, refresh_token: "refresh_token"} (the broken minimum schema strips the rest and injects the placeholder), and this spread overwrites o365AuthCredentials' real refresh token before the credential update persists it. The stored Office365 credential's refresh_token becomes the literal string "refresh_token" and its expiry timestamp is never updated (stale expiry forces a sync call on every operation); if credential sharing is later disabled or the endpoint removed, the credential can never refresh again and the user must re-authenticate.

adjudication.rationale: In `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` it uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema` which (a) does not include `refresh_token` and (b) is a plain `z.object(...)` (so unknown keys like expiry fields are stripped). The helper then force-injects `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when missing. In `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed data is merged via `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`, so the injected placeholder refresh_token can overwrite the real stored refresh token, and any expiry fields stripped by the minimal schema will not update, leaving stale expiry. This is directly grounded in the new helper + Office365 refresh logic.
